data.foodNote: Thighs are done at 165F, and they stay juicy past it. Dark meat forgives an extra few minutes where breast dries out.

description: Convert oven settings for chicken thighs to the air fryer: 425F for 40 minutes becomes either 400F for 40 minutes or 425F, check at 30. Pull at 165F.

examples.result: Either 400F for 40 minutes, or 425F and check at about 30 minutes.
steps: Write down the oven settings: 425F, 40 minutes.
Lower the temperature: 425 minus 25 is 400F, and the time stays 40 minutes.
Or shorten the time: 40 × 0.75 = 30 minutes, at the same 425F.

steps: Write down the oven settings: 400F, 35 minutes.

Or shorten the time: 35 × 0.75 = 26.25, rounded to 26 minutes, at the same 400F.

faqs.answer: Either 40 minutes at 400F or check at about 30 minutes at 425F, for bone-in thighs that roast for 40 minutes in the oven. Boneless thighs take about 20 minutes at 400F. Check about a quarter sooner for bone-in.
faqs.question: How long do chicken thighs take in the air fryer?

faqs.answer: Bone-in thighs do, because the bone insulates the meat. Boneless thighs cook in about the same time as a boneless breast.
faqs.question: Do thighs take longer than breasts?

faqs.answer: Skin side up. The heat comes from above, so skin that faces up crisps. Pat it dry first, and do not crowd the basket.
faqs.question: Should thighs be skin side up or down?

faqs.answer: Yes, and many cooks prefer them around 175F, where the texture is better. 165F is the safety minimum. Past that is a taste choice.
faqs.question: Can I cook thighs past 165F?

faqs.answer: Once, halfway, if you want even browning. Skin that stays up the whole cook comes out crisper, so flipping is optional for thighs.
faqs.question: Do I flip chicken thighs?

felicityNote: Thighs are the chicken I reach for on a tired night. They forgive a late timer, they forgive a hot fryer, and the skin always crisps.

parts.meaning: The air fryer runs hotter than the dial says, because the fan pushes hot air straight onto the food. Dropping 25F keeps the skin from burning before the meat cooks.
When you lower the temperature, the food still needs the full oven time. The lower heat and the full time balance each other out.
A quarter sooner. Keep the oven temperature and check at three quarters of the oven time. Open the basket then, look, and check the temperature.
The safe internal temperature for chicken, measured in the thickest part, away from the bone.

formula.text: Pick one, never both. Lower the temperature: air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F, and the time stays the same. Or shorten the time: keep the oven temperature and check at oven time × 0.75. For chicken thighs at 425F for 40 minutes: either 400F for 40 minutes, or 425F and check at about 30 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the oven settings
howToSteps.text: Find the temperature and time in your recipe. Bone-in thighs usually roast at 425F for 40 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Pick one change
howToSteps.text: Pick one change, not both. Either take 25F off the temperature and keep the time, or keep the temperature and check a quarter sooner. 425F for 40 minutes becomes either 400F for 40 minutes or 425F and check at about 30 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Dry and season
howToSteps.text: Pat the skin dry, season, and load the thighs skin side up in a single layer.

howToSteps.name: Cook and check
howToSteps.text: Pull the thighs when the thickest part reads 165F, and check about a quarter sooner if you kept the temperature.

lede: Bone-in thighs that roast at 425F for 40 minutes air fry two ways: 400F for the full 40 minutes, or 425F and check at about 30 minutes. Pull them when the thickest part reads 165F.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Chicken Thighs
tutorial: Thighs are the most forgiving chicken in the air fryer. Bone-in thighs that roast at 425F for 40 minutes air fry two ways: 400F for the full 40 minutes, or 425F and check at about 30 minutes. Either way the skin comes out crisper than the oven manages.

Dark meat forgives what breast does not. A thigh that cooks a few minutes past done stays juicy, because the fat and the connective tissue keep it moist. That makes thighs the chicken to learn the air fryer on. The converted time is a starting point, and a few minutes either way still gives you dinner.

Bone-in takes longer than boneless, and the bone is the reason. Bone insulates the meat around it, so a bone-in thigh needs the full oven time at the lower temperature, while a boneless thigh finishes sooner. The presets cover both. If you are converting a recipe, check whether it says bone-in or boneless before you trust the time.

Skin side up, and do not move them. Thighs go in skin side up, and the skin crisps under the heat from above. Flip them once halfway if the recipe says so, but skin that starts up and stays up comes out crisper. Pat the skin dry first, the same as wings.

The thermometer still decides. Thighs are done at 165F in the thickest part, away from the bone. Some cooks take dark meat higher, toward 175F, for better texture, and that is a taste choice, not a safety rule. The safety number is 165F, and the thermometer is the only honest test.
